note_on_method: Each venue page rests on one line of the City of Huntington Beach's Park Amenities page - a name, a street address and a court count under a heading that states the absence of lighting for all four parks - plus whatever other amenity lists on the same page name the park, the City's Tennis & Pickleball Information page for community-centre addresses and lighted tennis hours, and the US Census address geocoder for the county and the postcode. Where the City is silent, these pages record the silence.

slots.description:
One pickleball court, unlit, in a park the City lists for an exercise course and a volleyball court and very little else.

The City's whole record of this venue is one line on its Park Amenities page: "Boardwalk Park - 7441 Edinger Ave. - 1 Court". It sits under the heading "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)", which answers the lighting question for this park and the three others beneath it in one parenthesis. One court is the smallest count in Huntington Beach, and the smallest a venue can have and still be a venue.

The same page places Boardwalk Park on two other lists. It appears under "CITY PARKS WITH AN EXERCISE COURSE/FITNESS STATION", one of three parks in the city that do, and under "THE CITY PARKS WITH A VOLLEYBALL COURT". It does not appear under restrooms, basketball, tennis, picnic shelters or walking loops. Boardwalk is the only one of the four pickleball parks that the City does not list with a restroom, a basketball court or a sports field, which is as close as the City comes to telling you it is a small park.
slots.getting_there:
7441 Edinger Ave., Huntington Beach, CA 92647. The US Census address geocoder matched the address at house-number level as "7441 EDINGER AVE, HUNTINGTON BEACH, CA, 92647" and placed it in Orange County, in the incorporated place Huntington Beach city. It is the only one of the four published venues in the 92647 postcode; the four parks fall in four different postcodes between them.

The City publishes nothing about parking at this park, and its restroom list does not include Boardwalk Park. That second absence is recorded as unknown rather than as a no, because a list of parks with restrooms is not a list of parks without them.
slots.what_to_expect:
One court, which means one game at a time. Four players fill it and a fifth waits. There is no rotation to join and no second court to spill onto, so this is a venue for a group that arrives together, not for turning up alone hoping to find a game.

The court is unlit, and that is the City's statement rather than this site's guess: the heading over the line reads "(NO LIGHTING)". Play finishes with the daylight, whatever the season. The City publishes no hours for the court beyond that, no price, no surface and nothing about when it is used. It never calls the court indoor or outdoor, so these pages do not either.

What the park is listed for besides the court is an exercise course or fitness station and a volleyball court. If the one court is taken, the City's own list gives the alternatives: four courts each at Edison Park, Marina Park and Worthy Park, all equally unlit.

faqs.a: One. The City's line reads "Boardwalk Park - 7441 Edinger Ave. - 1 Court", the smallest count in Huntington Beach.
No, stated by the City: the heading over the count reads "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)". Play ends at dusk.
Not stated. The City prices reserved tennis courts and says nothing about the cost of pickleball, so this site records the fee as unknown rather than as free.
The City's list of parks with a restroom does not include Boardwalk Park. That is recorded here as unknown, not as a no.

faqs.q: What else is in the park?
faqs.a: The City lists Boardwalk Park for an exercise course or fitness station and a volleyball court. It does not list it for a basketball court, a sports field, tennis courts or a walking loop.

slots.description:
Four pickleball courts, unlit, in the park that shares its address with the Edison Community Center on Magnolia Street.

The City's line is "Edison Park - 21377 Magnolia St. - 4 Courts", under the heading "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)". Four courts is the largest count in Huntington Beach, shared with Marina Park and Worthy Park, and it is enough for two games at once.

On the City's amenities page Edison Park appears on more lists than any other pickleball park in the city: restroom, basketball court, handball court, skate park, sports field, tennis court, volleyball court and walking loop. The tennis courts are lit - the Tennis & Pickleball Information page lists "Edison Community Park (ECC)* 21377 Magnolia Street Dusk to 10 p.m. nightly", the asterisk marking a location with handball and racquetball courts - and the pickleball courts, on the City's other page, are explicitly not. The two records describe two different sets of courts at one address, and this page keeps them apart rather than letting the tennis hours leak onto the pickleball.
slots.getting_there:
21377 Magnolia St., Huntington Beach, CA 92646. The US Census address geocoder matched "21377 MAGNOLIA ST, HUNTINGTON BEACH, CA, 92646" at house-number level and placed it in Orange County, in the incorporated place Huntington Beach city. Verification changed only the punctuation of this address, from "Magnolia St" to "Magnolia St.", to match the City's line.

The Edison Community Center is at the same address, (714) 960-8870, and is one of the four places the City says a player can register in person for its tennis and pickleball programmes. The City publishes nothing about parking. There is a restroom, stated on the amenities page.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four courts and no lights. Two games can run side by side, or eight players can rotate without a long wait, and all of it ends at dusk because the City says so in the heading over the count.

The thing to be careful of at this address is the other set of courts. The City's tennis page gives Edison a lighted-court window of "Dusk to 10 p.m. nightly" and says tennis courts "may be reserved at the Murdy Community Center, (714) 960-8895, for $9 per hour". Both facts belong to tennis. The pickleball courts have no stated hours, no stated price and no stated reservation system, and this site records them as such rather than borrowing the tennis answers.

The City publishes no surface, no parking and nothing about busy periods, and never calls these courts indoor or outdoor. What it does offer is instruction: OC Racquet Sports runs clinics the City describes in terms of "tennis or pickleball goals", registered through the City's SANDS system or at the community centre on this site.

Not stated. The City prices reserved tennis courts at $9 per hour and says nothing about the cost of pickleball, so the fee is recorded here as unknown.
Yes. Edison Park is on the City's list of parks with a restroom, one of three pickleball parks in the city that are.

faqs.q: What else is in the park?
faqs.a: The City lists a basketball court, a handball court, a skate park, a sports field, tennis courts, a volleyball court and a walking loop, and the Edison Community Center is at the same address.

slots.description:
Four pickleball courts, unlit, in a park the City lists for a handball court and a horseshoe pit as well as a field and a basketball court.

The City's line reads "Marina Park - 5562 Cross Dr. - 4 Courts", under the heading "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)". Four courts ties Marina with Edison Park and Worthy Park for the largest count in Huntington Beach.

The amenities page lists Marina Park under restroom, basketball court, handball court, horseshoe pit, sports field, tennis court and walking loop. It is one of three parks in the city with a horseshoe pit and one of two with a handball court, the other being Edison. The tennis courts here are lit - "Marina Park (MCP)* 5562 Cross Drive Dusk to 10 p.m. nightly" on the Tennis & Pickleball Information page - and the pickleball courts are not, the same split as at Edison and the same reason to read the two City pages separately.

The City also gives Marina Park a second address, 15871 Graham Street, on the tennis page. That is the community centre where a player registers; the courts are at Cross Drive.
slots.getting_there:
5562 Cross Dr., Huntington Beach, CA 92649. The US Census address geocoder matched "5562 CROSS DR, HUNTINGTON BEACH, CA, 92649" at house-number level and placed it in Orange County, in the incorporated place Huntington Beach city.

The address to avoid for the courts is the other one the City publishes. Its tennis page lists "Marina Park 15871 Graham Street (714) 960-8895" among the community centres where a player can register in person, and the same page puts the lighted tennis courts at Cross Drive. The count-bearing address is Cross Drive, and that is the one published here. The City says nothing about parking. There is a restroom, stated on the amenities page.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four unlit courts, so two games at once and a hard stop at dusk. The City states the absence of lighting in the heading over the count, and it publishes no hours, no price and no surface for these courts.

The lit courts you may see at this park are tennis courts. The City's tennis page gives them "Dusk to 10 p.m. nightly" and prices a reservation at "$9 per hour" through the Murdy Community Center; neither the hours nor the price is stated for pickleball, and this site does not carry them across. Marina also carries the City's asterisk for handball and racquetball courts, and the amenities page adds a horseshoe pit, which is not something every pickleball venue on this site can say.

Registration for the City's tennis and pickleball programmes, including OC Racquet Sports clinics, is through the SANDS system or at the Marina Park community centre on Graham Street. Nothing is published about parking, busy periods, or whether the courts are indoor or outdoor.

faqs.a: Four. The City's line reads "Marina Park - 5562 Cross Dr. - 4 Courts", a count it shares with Edison Park and Worthy Park.
No, stated by the City under "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)". The courts at this park that are lit until 10 p.m. are tennis courts.
5562 Cross Dr. for the courts, which is the address the City pairs with the count. 15871 Graham Street, also published by the City for Marina Park, is the community centre for registrations.
Not stated. The City prices reserved tennis courts and never prices or frees a pickleball court, so the fee is recorded here as unknown.
Yes. Marina Park is on the City's list of parks with a restroom, and it is also listed for a handball court, a horseshoe pit, a basketball court, a sports field and a walking loop.

slots.description:
Four pickleball courts, unlit, in a park the City lists with a picnic table or shelter and no tennis courts.

The City's line is "Worthy Park - 1831 17th St. - 4 Courts", under the heading "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)". Four courts matches Edison Park and Marina Park for the largest count in the city.

Worthy is the one four-court venue in Huntington Beach that the City does not list under its tennis heading. Its amenities page puts the park on the restroom, basketball court, picnic table/shelter, sports field and walking loop lists, and on the pickleball list, but not on "THE CITY PARKS/FACILITIES WITH A TENNIS COURT". So the "Dusk to 10 p.m." tennis lighting that complicates the Edison and Marina pages does not arise here; there is nothing lit at Worthy in the City's record at all.

The park carries two City addresses. The amenities page pairs the count with 1831 17th St.; the Tennis & Pickleball Information page lists "Worthy Park 1801 Main Street" among the community centres that take registrations. Both are the City's, and the one paired with the count is the one published.
slots.getting_there:
1831 17th St., Huntington Beach, CA 92648. The US Census address geocoder matched "1831 17TH ST, HUNTINGTON BEACH, CA, 92648" at house-number level and placed it in Orange County, in the incorporated place Huntington Beach city.

The City also publishes 1801 Main Street for this park, with the phone number (714) 960-8884, on its tennis page. Both addresses are the City's; the 17th Street one is paired with the court count, so it is the one published here, and the imported record that previously carried Main Street was overridden by it. The City publishes nothing about parking. There is a restroom, stated on the amenities page.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four courts, no lights, and no tennis courts to confuse the picture. Two games can run at once, and play ends at dusk on the City's own statement.

Because Worthy does not appear on the City's tennis list, none of the tennis page's numbers - the 10 p.m. lighting window, the $9 reservation - has anything to attach to at this park. What the tennis page does say about Worthy is that it is a community centre where a player can register in person for the City's tennis and pickleball programmes, at the Main Street address.

The amenities page lists a picnic table or shelter here, which none of the other three pickleball parks has, along with a restroom, a basketball court, a sports field and a walking loop. The City publishes no surface, no price, no hours beyond the absence of lighting, nothing about parking and nothing about when the courts are busy, and it never calls them indoor or outdoor.

faqs.a: Four. The City's line reads "Worthy Park - 1831 17th St. - 4 Courts", the same count as Edison Park and Marina Park.
No, stated by the City under "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)". Worthy is not on the City's tennis list either, so nothing at this park is lit in the City's record.

faqs.q: Why does the City give two addresses?
faqs.a: 1831 17th St. is paired with the court count on the amenities page; 1801 Main Street is listed on the tennis page as the community centre for registrations. The 17th Street address is the one published here.
Not stated. The City prices reserved tennis courts and says nothing about the cost of pickleball, so the fee is recorded here as unknown.
Yes. Worthy Park is on the City's list of parks with a restroom, and it is the only one of the four pickleball parks listed with a picnic table or shelter.
